definition: Harvey is a generative artificial intelligence (AI) product developed by the Counsel AI Corporation for the legal industry.
details: The product has been described as a provider of customised large language models (LLMs) for law firms and in-house legal teams. It is named after the lead character of the legal drama Suits, Harvey Specter.

explainer.lead: Harvey is generative AI software built for legal work by Counsel AI Corporation. It gives law firms and in-house legal teams access to customised large language models rather than a one-size-fits-all legal chatbot.

tiers.eli5: Harvey is like a writing and reading helper trained for people who work with law. A legal team can ask it for help, but a lawyer still needs to check its work. Its name comes from Harvey Specter, the lead character in the television drama Suits.
tiers.practitioner: Harvey is applied as a customised LLM product within law firms and in-house legal teams. Users should treat its generated text as assistance, not authoritative legal advice, and have qualified lawyers review outputs before relying on them.
tiers.paperLevel: Harvey is a generative AI product developed by Counsel AI Corporation for the legal industry, described as providing customised large language models to law firms and in-house legal teams. It is a product-level system rather than a named model architecture or benchmark.

explainer.example: A lawyer asks Harvey to help produce an initial summary of a lengthy legal document. The lawyer then checks the summary against the original document before sharing it with colleagues.

usedIn.name: Law firms

usedIn.name: In-house legal teams
usedIn.detail: Generative AI assistance within an organisation’s legal function.

explainer.intuition: The idea is to adapt the broad abilities of a large language model to the needs of legal organisations. Harvey packages that capability as a dedicated product for legal professionals.
howItWorks: A lawyer or legal team brings a legal task to Harvey.
The product processes the request using a customised large language model.
Harvey generates a response or draft for the legal team.
Legal professionals review the output before using it in their work.
explainer.whyItMatters: Harvey applies generative AI directly to professional legal settings, where customised tools may fit organisational needs better than general-purpose software. It also shows why human review remains important when generated text informs legal work.
misconceptions: Harvey is not a lawyer or law firm; it is an AI software product.
It is not named after a technical method: its name references Harvey Specter from Suits.
A customised model does not make every generated answer legally correct.
